one_line: Last great ruler of the Hindu Shahi dynasty, leading a doomed resistance from the Salt Range and Siwalik hills against Mahmud’s Ghaznavid invasions in the early 11th century.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s to early 40s, lean but battle-hardened, with a disciplined warrior’s posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a prominent straight nose, medium wheat-brown complexion weathered by sun, high cheekbones, neatly trimmed full beard and moustache, a faint old scar running diagonally across his left cheek; default expression calm, resolute and slightly melancholy, with sharp, watchful eyes.
appearance.hair: Thick, dark brown hair gathered into a high, neat warrior topknot at the back of the crown, sides smoothed back; no shaved portions; a narrow, dark red cloth headband tied around the forehead, and a simple, low golden circlet (plain band, no large gems) worn over the headband.
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length tunic (anga) of sturdy undyed off‑white cotton with very fine red edging at the cuffs and hem, belted at the waist with a broad dark brown leather girdle; over this, a fitted dark indigo quilted cotton coat-of-plates style jacket (padded, with faint vertical stitching) reaching mid‑thigh, open at the front but fastened by three simple leather ties, allowing the off‑white tunic to show; his lower body is clad in narrow, slightly tapered churidar-style trousers in muted earthy brown tucked into mid‑calf high brown leather boots with plain lacing; over one shoulder he wears a dusty, travel‑worn woollen shawl in muted brick red, draped from his left shoulder across his torso and pinned near the right hip, evoking a prince in exile rather than a courtly king; his arms are protected by simple brown leather bracers with a few small bronze studs, and he wears minimal jewellery—a single small gold earring in each ear and a thin gold torque at the neck, signalling royal status but in restrained, practical form.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved, single‑edged Indian sword (early talwar‑like) with a modest steel blade, plain iron crossguard, and simple dark wood hilt wrapped in brown leather, sheathed in a dark brown scabbard that hangs from his leather girdle on the left; in hand, he often rests it point‑down beside him, symbolising stubborn but ultimately doomed resistance.

ref_desc: Trilochanapala is a late‑30s, lean, wheat‑brown, oval‑faced Hindu Shahi king with a neat beard, scar on his left cheek, dark brown hair in a high topknot with a red headband and simple gold circlet, wearing an off‑white tunic under a dark indigo quilted jacket, brown churidar trousers, brick red shawl, brown leather boots and bracers, and carrying a plain slightly curved Indian sword in a dark brown scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style model sheet of Trilochanapala as a historically grounded early 11th‑century Hindu Shahi king from the Salt Range: a late‑30s, lean but battle‑hardened man with wheat‑brown skin, oval face, high cheekbones, a straight nose, a neat full beard and moustache, and a faint diagonal scar on his left cheek, his default expression calm, resolute and slightly sad; his thick dark brown hair is pulled into a high, tidy topknot, the sides smoothed back, with a narrow dark red cloth headband tied around his forehead and a simple slim gold circlet resting over it. Show him in a long‑sleeved, knee‑length off‑white cotton tunic with fine red trim on cuffs and hem, belted with a broad dark brown leather girdle; over this, a fitted dark indigo quilted cotton jacket with visible vertical stitching, reaching mid‑thigh and fastened by three leather ties at the chest, the tunic visible beneath. His trousers are narrow, slightly wrinkled earthy brown churidar‑style, tucked into mid‑calf high brown leather boots with modest lacing; a muted brick red woollen shawl is draped from his left shoulder across his torso and pinned near the right hip, worn like a practical cloak of a king in exile, not a courtly robe. Add simple brown leather bracers with a few bronze studs, a thin gold torque at his neck, and one small gold earring in each ear. His signature weapon is a slightly curved single‑edged Indian sword (early talwar‑like) with a plain steel blade, modest iron crossguard, and dark wood hilt wrapped in brown leather, hanging in a dark brown scabbard from his belt on the left; include a view with him holding it point‑down by his side. Use a palette dominated by off‑white, dark indigo, brick red, earthy brown, and dark brown leather, keeping the overall look dignified, practical, and historically plausible for a last‑stand hill‑fort warrior‑king, with clear front, side, and rear views to fix his hair, costume and weapon details.
